summary: New Jersey inspectors found 62 unpermitted natural-gas generators powering a large AI data center in Vineland. The state fined the operator $1.07 million, and residents complained about noise and emissions.
technical_summary: A hyperscale data center serving AI computing demand installed off-grid natural-gas generators without required air permits to get power faster than the grid could supply it. Regulators found the violation and fined the operator.

failure_mode.quote: None of the 2,000-kilowatt natural-gas-powered generators had the required permits to be installed or to operate at the site.

affected_population.quote: The complex is near farmland, homes and two schools.

notes: Infrastructure and permitting incident rather than an AI system malfunction; health effects of emissions are not documented.

summary: Weibo's moderation system struggled to keep up as Chinese users invented new slang and puns to get around state censorship. The report describes the evolving language games rather than a specific harm.
technical_summary: A platform moderation model that filters banned topics is evaded by constantly changing homophones, puns, emoji and character play. The shifting vocabulary degrades detection, a distribution-shift weakness in keyword- and language-based moderation.

failure_mode.quote: allowing netizens to use the humor and cleverness of spoken Mandarin to dodge censorship

notes: The excerpt covers user evasion of censorship and does not describe the moderation model directly.

summary: An AI-generated video of tigers on a West Bengal madrasa campus went viral, causing panic among parents and students and a sharp drop in attendance. A teacher at the school said he made it to teach students about AI fakes.
technical_summary: A teacher used generative AI tools to produce a realistic video of tigers on school grounds and it spread on Facebook. Viewers took it as real, prompting safety fears. The creator said it was an awareness exercise.

technology.quote: An AI-generated video showing three tigers on a madrasa campus at Barasat went viral on Wednesday

harm_type.quote: causing panic among students and guardians and leading to a sharp drop in attendance

affected_population.quote: causing panic among students and guardians and leading to a sharp drop in attendance

notes: Creator's stated intent was educational, so malicious_use is a loose fit for deliberate deceptive use.

summary: Fable's AI-generated year-end reading summaries produced biased and offensive remarks about users' race, gender, sexuality and disability. The company apologized and removed the feature.
technical_summary: Fable used OpenAI's API to write playful 'roast' style recaps of users' reading. The model produced combative comments about race and identity despite an offensive-language filter, which the company said failed. The feature was later withdrawn.

technology.quote: Fable hopped on the trend by using OpenAI’s API to generate summaries

failure_mode.quote: reader summaries that were offensive to race, gender, sexuality and disability
Clearly in both cases, that failed this time around

harm_type.quote: We are deeply sorry for the hurt caused by some of our Reader Summaries this week

affected_population.quote: reader summaries that were offensive to race, gender, sexuality and disability

summary: Online trolls used AI voice synthesis to imitate video game voice actors, reading out the actors' home addresses and racist and abusive statements, then posted the clips on Twitter.
technical_summary: Harassers cloned the voices of several voice actors from publicly available recordings using a commercial voice synthesis service. They then generated clips containing private addresses and offensive content and spread them on social media.

technology.quote: Artificial intelligence-generated voices are already being used to harass ordinary people

failure_mode.quote: online trolls creating the voices and then having them read out

summary: South Korean police arrested a man for sharing an AI-generated image of an escaped zoo wolf on a city street. Authorities used the fake image in an emergency alert and briefing and moved their search.
technical_summary: A man used a generative image tool to insert the escaped wolf into a street photo and shared it. The image was treated as genuine, triggering an emergency text and redirecting search operations until police traced him through camera footage and AI usage records.

technology.quote: sharing an AI-generated image that misled authorities who were searching for a wolf

harm_type.quote: prompted authorities to urgently relocate their search operation
The AI-generated image of Neukgu had prompted Daejeon city government to issue an emergency text to residents

notes: The report says the man acted for fun; the use of ChatGPT comes from the AIID description.

summary: A TikTok account posted 14 AI-generated videos styled as television news ahead of Kosovo's December 2025 elections. They favored one party and made election and diaspora claims, reaching hundreds of thousands of views.
technical_summary: An account used generative video tools, with a visible Sora logo, to produce news-style clips with synthetic presenters and imagery. The format made partisan claims look like reporting, although TikTok labeled the videos as AI-generated.

technology.quote: Through the style of television news reports, a TikTok account has published dozens of videos generated by artificial intelligence

harm_type.quote: it is noticeable that the content favors the political entity, the Vetëvendosje Movement

notes: Videos carried an AI label; intent and actual influence on voters are not established.

summary: Security researchers showed that Tesla's Autopilot lane recognition could be tricked by crafted adversarial inputs and that the car could be controlled remotely with a gamepad. Tesla questioned how practical the attacks were.
technical_summary: Researchers demonstrated adversarial samples that confuse the lane-detection vision system and a remote-control exploit. No real-world harm was reported, and the incident was later reclassified as an issue rather than an incident.
notes: The only report is an index of incidents downgraded to issues, so all tags rely on the AIID description.

summary: Facebook's automated moderation marked dozens of wildfire emergency posts as spam and removed them, including posts from fire agencies and a fire alert app. Users were not notified of the removals.
technical_summary: Facebook's spam detection flagged posts with links or screenshots from official and volunteer wildfire sources as attempts to get likes or shares. The classifier misjudged emergency content, and affected users received no notice of removal.
systems: Facebook spam and content moderation system

technology.quote: Facebook has been flagging and removing dozens of posts containing links and screenshots

failure_mode.quote: None of the users were notified that their posts were removed.

harm_type.quote: Facebook is reportedly taking down important safety information as wildfire season spreads across the western part of the country.

notes: No specific injury is documented; the risk is reduced access to evacuation and fire information.

summary: Queens prosecutors charged a former City Council candidate with forgery for allegedly using AI to create fake endorsements, fabricated news articles and videos, and false claims that an opponent had withdrawn.
technical_summary: The candidate allegedly used generative AI image, video and text tools to alter genuine endorsement graphics and produce fake news posts with real outlets' branding, then posted them on campaign social media to simulate support and mislead voters.
systems: Generative AI image and video tools

sector.quote: a deliberate effort to mislead voters ahead of a City Council election

technology.quote: routinely and deliberately created and posted AI-generated images on his official social media accounts

failure_mode.quote: routinely and deliberately created and posted AI-generated images on his official social media accounts

harm_type.quote: a deliberate effort to mislead voters ahead of a City Council election

affected_population.quote: a deliberate effort to mislead voters ahead of a City Council election

notes: Allegations from prosecutors; the charges are not proven.

summary: South Africa's Home Affairs department found apparently AI-generated fictitious references attached to a Cabinet-approved white paper on citizenship and immigration. It suspended two senior officials and ordered a review of its policy documents.
technical_summary: A reference list for a policy paper contained fabricated sources attributed to large language model hallucination, added after the document was written and not cited in the text. No verification step caught it before approval and publication.
deployers: South African Department of Home Affairs

failure_mode.quote: It seems that these references were generated and attached to the document after the fact
AI-generated citations were included without proper verification

harm_type.quote: The Department nonetheless sincerely apologises for this unacceptable oversight.

notes: The department says the body of the paper is not materially affected.

summary: Amazon's AI-generated review summary described Mein Kampf as 'a true work of art', and Google's search then displayed that summary as a featured snippet for a search about positive reviews.
technical_summary: An AI model summarizing customer reviews on a product page produced a misleadingly positive characterization of the book. Google's search algorithm then surfaced that AI summary as a featured snippet, a system summarizing another system's output.

technology.quote: So, it's a search algorithm attempting to summarize an AI summary.

failure_mode.quote: Readers describe the book as a true work of art.
